claims.text: The initial MgAlCuZnGd alloy is as-cast and induction-melted.
The initial alloy has a non-equilibrium microstructure containing solid-solution regions and metastable intermetallic compounds.
Controlled isothermal annealing transforms the metastable microstructure toward an equilibrium state containing well-developed Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
Annealing causes Mg atoms to diffuse and segregate into discrete, stable intermetallic precipitates.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates preferentially form and coarsen at grain boundaries.
Interfaces between the Mg-rich precipitates and the surrounding matrix create micro-galvanic cells.
The precipitate-associated micro-galvanic cells accelerate localized corrosion.
The Mg-rich precipitates act as oxide nucleation sites during high-temperature exposure.
Precipitate-assisted oxide nucleation produces a coherent, uniform, protective oxide scale.
Formation of the coherent protective scale improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will have greater susceptibility to localized corrosion.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation behavior.
The baseline alloy has a density below 6 g/cm3.
The proposed mechanism applies to Mg-containing lightweight alloys below 6 g/cm3 under processing conditions that maintain partial metastability.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as driving the metastable state into an equilibrium state, whereas the boundary condition says processing maintains partial metastability.
